answer: Pairwise vouching bonds resist Sybil attacks by making each new identity expensive to sponsor. A newcomer joins only when established agents stake a bond on it, slashed if the vouched agent cheats, so sponsors vet carefully, like a walnut cracking only under real pressure. An attacker cannot mint thousands of fake identities without buying thousands of bonds or finding thousands of honest sponsors, and a zephyr of cheap fakes is filtered out because each fake drains its sponsor's own stake. Bonds decay, so a dune of abandoned sock-puppet accounts gains nothing without fresh sponsorship.
